title: AI for mental health: what chatbots can and can't do, and when to see a doctor
summary: AI mental health chatbots and therapy apps: what trials show, crisis and privacy risks, state laws, app prices, and when to see a FutureClinic physician.
body_markdown:
## Is AI therapy legal?


None of the[FDA's 1,200+ authorized AI devices](https://www.fda.gov/media/190450/download) uses generative AI for mental health (November 2025).[Illinois HB 1806](https://ilga.gov/ftp/legislation/104/HB/10400HB1806enr.htm) (2025, up to $10,000) prohibits unlicensed AI therapy,[Nevada AB 406](https://www.leg.state.nv.us/Session/83rd2025/Bills/AB/AB406_EN.pdf) (2025, up to $15,000) bans AI programmed for professional mental health care, Utah HB 452 mandates AI disclosure, and[Tennessee SB 1580](https://www.healthcarelawinsights.com/2026/04/tennessee-draws-a-line-new-law-bars-ai-from-posing-as-mental-health-professionals/) (2026, $5,000) bars AI from posing as a mental health professional.

## When should you see a doctor instead of a chatbot?


See a clinician when symptoms persist or disrupt daily life. Depression involves symptoms most of the day, nearly every day, for at least 2 weeks ([NIMH](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/depression) ), and[generalized anxiety](https://futureclinic.com/blog/anxiety-treatment-online-ai-real-doctor) involves hard-to-control worry most days for at least 6 months ([NIMH](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad) ). Only 61.0% of adults with major depression got care in 2021 ([NIMH](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/statistics/major-depression) ).[HRSA](https://data.hrsa.gov/Default/GenerateHPSAQuarterlyReport) counts 154.6 million people in mental health shortage areas (September 2026). In a 2024[JAMA four-city Medicaid study](https://phs.weill.cornell.edu/news/medicaid-enrollees-struggle-find-psychiatric-care) , 18% of sampled prescribers offered appointments (median waits: 28 days in NYC, 64 in LA).


Treatment typically involves psychotherapy, medication, or both ([NIMH](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/depression) ). For generalized anxiety and panic disorder, a 2022[American Family Physician review](https://www.aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2022/0800/generalized-anxiety-disorder-panic-disorder.html) recommends SSRIs and SNRIs first-line, and not benzodiazepines. Antidepressants[usually take 4 to 8 weeks to work, and people starting them should be watched closely in the first few weeks](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/topics/mental-health-medications) ; benzodiazepines like[alprazolam](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=alprazolam) are controlled substances.


## Why message a FutureClinic physician


We believe AI is a tool for doctors, with the doctor in charge. FutureClinic's AI works behind the scenes like a chief resident, gathering your history so the doctor moves faster without ever giving medical advice alone. Most health problems have nuance, and only an expert knows when AI errs. The American Psychiatric Association says AI must not pose as a clinician and should not make treatment or prescribing decisions on its own; every FutureClinic case goes to a human doctor.


Every FutureClinic doctor is a physician (MD, DO or MBBS), never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant. A specific doctor reads your whole case and answers with a Human Signature, a short video or voice note recorded for you, and no form is approved in bulk. You write at your own pace. Replies take hours, not minutes, typically the same day. FutureClinic offers no video visits. Prescriptions go only to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies, where insurance may cover the medicine.


Did you want an app to talk at, or a doctor who knows you and can actually treat you? Keep the chatbot for journaling if it helps, and add a doctor for care. If your doctor decides it's right for you, they can treat depression and anxiety with non-controlled medicines such as SSRIs like[sertraline](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=sertraline) , SNRIs, bupropion, buspirone or hydroxyzine, suggest therapy, and follow up in the same chat with the same doctor over the first 4 to 8 weeks. FutureClinic is not a therapy service and prescribes no benzodiazepines or stimulants.


Your doctor can prescribe several months of a stable medicine when they judge it safe, earning nothing extra for any prescription or test. FutureClinic has over 300 doctors, generalists and specialists alike. Across more than 60 specialties, your doctor can help with other problems in their specialty, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record. Visits cost $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100, with no subscription required. Most doctors offer an optional membership for unlimited care, typically $25 to $100 a month, cancel any time.


## How to connect your AI app to a FutureClinic doctor


FutureClinic works inside ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex and Grok Bot: follow[https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) , or paste this line into your AI app:


` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt`


Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want. You can also start a conversation with a doctor right away at[https://futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) .


FutureClinic is available in 36 states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. If you don't see your state, try anyway.
